clinical_significance.statement: The caption identifies intercellular epidermal IgG staining on DIF. The case considered pemphigus after positive DIF but excluded it using morphology and negative autoantibody/IIF workup, so fluorescence positivity is not a confirmed pemphigus diagnosis.

evidence.quote: C) Intraepidermal intercellular IgG deposition with a “net-like” pattern.
Further examination of specific anti-skin autoantibodies, particularly anti-Dsg1 and anti-Dsg3 antibodies, was negative, as was indirect immunofluorescence.

Furthermore, the presence of dyskeratosis associated with prominent suprabasal intraepidermal acantholysis, with a “dilapidated brick wall” appearance, and the absence of prominent inflammation excluded the diagnosis of pemphigus in our case.

limitations: Antibody identity and direct-immunofluorescence technique come from the source caption, not green color alone.
The caption identifies IgG; the image does not identify an independent C3 channel or establish the pemphigus diagnosis.
